writing.explanation:
A problem is a good match for Suffix Array when it asks for substring order, repeated substrings, offline text indexes. Here the concrete task is: Return suffix starting indexes in lexicographic order. The visible input `banana` is an example, not a definition of the whole problem. Ask what operations the solution must support and what the input guarantees. Look for repeated prefix queries or pattern matching before choosing a trie or preprocessing; a one-off short search may not need either. The right choice follows from those guarantees, not from a familiar noun in the prompt.

The decisive invariant is: Sort suffix ranks by doubling compared prefix length until every suffix has a unique rank. Try to say why it applies to the task without quoting the implementation. Which fact becomes known after one update, and which possible answers remain? String algorithms compare symbols or prefixes, but a Rust String is UTF-8 bytes. State whether the task means bytes, scalar values, or grapheme clusters. If that claim cannot be maintained on a legal input, the pattern is wrong or one of its preconditions is missing. A counterexample is more useful than a vague warning: change one property of the sample, trace the first two steps, and identify the exact claim that fails.

Compare costs before committing. The advertised bound is O(n log^2 n) simple · O(n log n) tuned; identify the operation responsible for it and the extra memory it needs. Then compare a straightforward alternative: a direct scan, full sort, or repeated recomputation may be easier but can pay for the same work many times. Do not choose the more elaborate method just because it has a famous name. For the sample, predict `5,3,1,0,4,2` and explain which part of the state lets the method reach that result.

When the prompt is ambiguous, ask about input size, ordering, duplicates, and required output format. Test empty pattern and text, repeated characters, overlapping matches, and non-ASCII input if the contract allows it. Use bytes only when the input contract permits byte-wise matching. Never index a String as though every character occupied one byte. The Rust sketch can show a useful primitive without proving that the whole task is solved; connect each primitive to the requested output. You should be able to name a fitting case, a near miss, and the assumption separating them before writing the first line.
